summary:
The "Cardiomyopathy Health Education, Awareness, and Research, and AED Training in the Schools Act of 2024" (or the "HEARTS Act of 2024"), Public Law 118-176, amends the Public Health Service Act (PHSA) (42 U.S.C. 201 et seq.) to expand federal initiatives, research, and educational resources regarding pediatric and adult cardiomyopathy and related cardiac conditions. 

Section 2(a) of the Act inserts four new sections—312A through 312D (42 U.S.C. 244a–244d)—after section 312 of the PHSA:

*   **Section 312A (42 U.S.C. 244a) - Education and Awareness Materials:** Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS), in consultation with the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to develop public education materials on high-risk cardiac conditions, automated external defibrillator (AED) placement guidelines, cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training, and cardiac emergency response plans within 18 months of enactment. Within 30 months of enactment, the Secretary must disseminate these materials to State educational agencies (SEAs), health departments, and medical professionals, and post them on the CDC website. SEAs are encouraged to distribute these resources to school personnel, families, and caregivers.
*   **Section 312B (42 U.S.C. 244b) - CDC Reporting and Risk Assessments:** Requires the Secretary, acting through the CDC Director, to submit a public report to Congress within 18 months of enactment on the prevalence, epidemiology, and natural history of cardiomyopathy, subject to federal and state privacy laws. It also mandates that the Secretary develop a public cardiomyopathy risk assessment tool (including worksheets and screening guidelines) in consultation with external stakeholders, including patient advocacy organizations and medical societies.
*   **Section 312C (42 U.S.C. 244c) - NIH Research Coordination:** Grants discretionary authority to the Secretary, in consultation with the Director of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), to expand and coordinate NIH research on cardiomyopathy etiology, longitudinal outcomes, and treatments, subject to a statutory nonduplication mandate. It establishes an 18-month deadline for the Secretary to submit a report to Congress outlining ongoing NIH research and defining adult and pediatric research agendas.
*   **Section 312D (42 U.S.C. 244d) - AED and CPR Grant Program:** Authorizes the Secretary to award discretionary grants to local educational agencies (LEAs)—acting in consultation with qualified tax-exempt or public healthcare entities—to establish comprehensive AED and CPR programs in public elementary and secondary schools. Permissible uses of funds include purchasing FDA-approved or cleared AEDs, maintaining equipment, and training school communities.

Section 2(b) of the Act contains a funding limitation, specifying that no additional funds are authorized to be appropriated to carry out these new PHSA provisions.
